_doc: Business addresses for the ads page (build_ads.py), read from the ad itself (crop image or OCR of the same ad), as printed. Keyed like ad_crops.json: issue + page + headline. 'address' is a list; each entry shows on its own line at the top of the ad card, plain text, never linked. An ad with no address has no entry. Uncertain parts are left out here (the public page shows no VERIFY) and listed in 'uncertain'.
uncertain: CR_1855-02-01 p3 Smith, Whipper: U. A. Widal's house number, 303 or 308 Lombard (left out)
CR_1861-01-19 p3 Peer: house number, 80 1/2 or 90 1/2 South Street (left out)
CR_1861-01-26 p3 Duterte: 634 Lombard, faint here; OCR of this printing family gives 634 and 631 (left out)
CR_1861-02-09 p3 Allmond: faint here, shown as 1027 because the repeat printings and the Johnson and Ware ad read 1027
CR_1861-02-23 p3 Burris: house number illegible in every printing, North 11th (left out)
CR_1861-05-04 p3 Downs: looks like 285 here, 225 on the May 18 printing and most repeats (number left out)
CR_1861-07-06 p3 Palmer: house number faint, probably 105 North Fifth (left out)
CR_1861-11-16 p3 Johnson and Ware: Mrs. Jane Johnson's residence, about 616 S. 9th St. (left out)
CR_1862-02-01 p3 Burris concert: Franklin Hall on Sixth or Ninth street (street left out)
FJ_1828-05-30 p7 Gracy Jones: No. 8 1/2 South Fourth, fraction not certain (left out)
FJ_1828-05-30 p8 Richard Johnson: No. 111 or 114 Varick-Street (left out)
FJ_1828-06-13 p7 Eliza Johnson: No. 24 or 28 Elizabeth street (left out). The ad's dateline appears to read Philadelphia, not New York

CR_1862-09-06 p3 Jane Johnson: the ad and the Sept. 6 reading notice give 618 South 8th St.; the Sept. 27 contraband relief committee list prints 'Mrs. Jane Johnson, No. 618 South St.' (ad address kept as printed in the ad)
CR_1862-07-05 p3 Banaker House: proprietor printed 'Mrs. AMIA WILLIAM, of Cape May' (possibly Anna Williams); no street given
